title: Supplemental Material for Grossman et al, 2025
author: Nina T. Grossman
license_note: figshare article detail endpoint license.name: CC BY 4.0
materials: RNA sequencing Cultures were grown by inoculating conidia from strain JHH-5317 into 25 ml of RPMI to a concentration of 107 conidia/ml, incubating the flasks at 37°C in 5% CO2 to facilitate germination for four hours, then shaking them for 13 h at 37°C in atmospheric conditions. Following this, 25 ml of RPMI containing 16 mg/ml of ITR, 16 mg/ml of VRC, 8 mg/ml of AMB or 2% DMSO by volume were added to each flask, for final concentrations of 8 mg/ml ITR, 8 mg/ml VRC, 4 mg/ml AMB or 1% DMSO. Flasks were shaken at 37°C for two hours, then strained through Whatman #2 filters (Cytiva, Marlborough, MA), washed twice with sterile Milli-Q water, added to 2 ml of Trizol Reagent (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA), flash-frozen and stored at -80°C. Three biological replicates were performed. All drugs were obtained from MilliporeSigma (Burlington, MA) and dissolved in DMSO. Cell homogenization was performed in Trizol Reagent using silica spheres (Lysing Matrix C, MP Biomedicals, Irvine, CA) in a FastPrep 120 (MP Biomedicals), with 4 intervals at speed 6 for 30 sec. Homogenates remained on ice between shakes. Total RNA was purified using a PureLink RNA Mini Kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific), with the on-column PureLink DNase treatment, according to manufacturer’s instructions. RNA was quantified using a NanoDrop

Quality assessment was performed by RNA ScreenTape Analysis in a TapeStation 2200 (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA). Libraries for RNA-seq were prepared from 250 ng Total RNA using the Illumina TruSeq Stranded mRNA Library Prep kit, according to manufacturer’s Low Sample protocol (Illumina, San Diego, CA). Quality assessment of libraries was conducted by High Sensitivity ScreenTape analysis on a TapeStation 2200 (Agilent Technologies). Libraries were quantified by qPCR with the Kapa Library Quantification kit (Roche, Basel, Switzerland) in a StepOne Plus Real Time PCR System (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Libraries were diluted and pooled and a final quality assessment was performed using High Sensitivity DNA LabChip Analysis on a BioAnalyzer 2100 (Agilent Technologies). A paired end, 2 x 100bp, Illumina HiSeq 2500 run was performed at Johns Hopkins Genomics Genetic Resources Core Facility, RRID:SCR_018669. Genome annotation RNA sequencing reads were aligned to each of the three genome assemblies using HISAT2 version 2.2.1 (Kim et al.

steps.title: Inoculate conidia into RPMI
steps.instruction: Add conidia from strain JHH‑5317 to 25 mL RPMI to achieve 1 × 10⁷ conidia · mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Germinate cultures under CO₂
steps.instruction: Incubate flasks at 37 °C in 5 % CO₂ for 4 h to allow germination.

steps.title: Extended shaking incubation
steps.instruction: Continue shaking cultures at 37 °C for 13 h under atmospheric conditions.

steps.title: Add drug‑containing RPMI and incubate
steps.instruction: Prepare 25 mL RPMI containing 16 mg mL⁻¹ itraconazole (ITR), 16 mg mL⁻¹ voriconazole (VRC), 8 mg mL⁻¹ amphotericin B (AMB) or 2 % DMSO (v/v). Add to each flask to reach final concentrations of 8 mg mL⁻¹ ITR, 8 mg mL⁻¹ VRC, 4 mg mL⁻¹ AMB, or 1 % DMSO. Shake at 37 °C for 2 h.

steps.title: Filter, wash, and add Trizol
steps.instruction: Strain cultures through Whatman #2 filters (Cytiva), wash the retained material twice with sterile Milli‑Q water, transfer to 2 mL Trizol Reagent (Thermo Fisher), flash‑freeze, and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Homogenize cells in Trizol
steps.instruction: Place the Trizol‑containing samples in a FastPrep 120 with Lysing Matrix C silica spheres (MP Biomedicals) and perform 4 intervals at speed 6 for 30 s each, keeping homogenates on ice between shakes.

steps.title: Purify total RNA
steps.instruction: Extract RNA using PureLink RNA Mini Kit (Thermo Fisher) with on‑column PureLink DNase treatment, following the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Quantify RNA
steps.instruction: Measure RNA concentration with a NanoDrop spectrophotometer.

steps.title: Assess RNA quality
steps.instruction: Run RNA ScreenTape analysis on an Agilent TapeStation 2200.

steps.title: Prepare stranded mRNA libraries
steps.instruction: Use 250 ng total RNA to construct libraries with Illumina TruSeq Stranded mRNA Library Prep kit, following the Low Sample protocol.

steps.title: Check library quality
steps.instruction: Perform High Sensitivity ScreenTape analysis on the TapeStation 2200.

steps.title: Quantify libraries by qPCR
steps.instruction: Quantify each library using Kapa Library Quantification kit (Roche) on a StepOne Plus Real‑Time PCR System (Thermo Fisher).

steps.title: Pool libraries and final QC
steps.instruction: Dilute libraries to equal molarity, pool them, and assess the pool with High Sensitivity DNA LabChip on an Agilent BioAnalyzer 2100.

steps.title: Sequence libraries
steps.instruction: Run a paired‑end 2 × 100 bp Illumina HiSeq 2500 sequencing at Johns Hopkins Genomics Genetic Resources Core Facility (RRID:SCR_018669).

steps.title: Align reads with HISAT2
steps.instruction: Align RNA‑seq reads to each of the three genome assemblies using HISAT2 version 2.2.1.

steps.title: Assemble transcripts with Stringtie
steps.instruction: Input the HISAT2 alignments into Stringtie to generate transcript assemblies.

steps.title: Align protein database with tblastn
steps.instruction: Align 8 390 Microascaceae family proteins from GenBank to each genome using NCBI tblastn version 2.13.0+.

steps.title: Generate preliminary CDS with exonerate
steps.instruction: Cluster the tblastn alignments and run exonerate in protein2genome mode to produce preliminary coding‑sequence features.

steps.title: Reconcile features and produce GFF
steps.instruction: Filter and reconcile transcript and protein alignment features using gffcompare and gffread, outputting the final annotation in GFF format.

steps.title: Blast proteins against UniProtKB
steps.instruction: Extract the predicted protein sequences and align them to the UniProtKB database with blastp (accessed 01/2024), retaining the single best hit for each protein.
